headline: Scotland’s Largest Wilderness: National Park Travel Notice
reservation: Entry to the park is generally free, but specific activities like the bridge-based bungee jump or guided wildlife tours require third-party bookings. Camping and campervan stays are subject to specific local rules, including a fire byelaw that bans barbecues and open flames. Travelers should check with the Park Authority regarding path closures or seasonal stalking restrictions.

days.title: Highland Living and Heritage

stops.name: Highland Folk Museum
stops.detail: Explore the park's history through traditional buildings and outdoor exhibits near Newtonmore.

stops.name: Spey Bridge
stops.detail: View the aerial landscape of this historic river crossing and the surrounding flood plains.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours for local transfers; conditions vary
days.note: Expect higher visitor volumes in major communities like Aviemore and Grantown-on-Spey.

days.title: Mountains and Ancient Pine Forests

stops.name: Abernethy Forest
stops.detail: Visit this National Nature Reserve to look for red squirrels and crested tits in ancient woodlands.

stops.name: Cairngorm Mountain Railway
stops.detail: Gain perspective on the arctic-alpine plateau and the highest range of mountains in the UK.

days.driving: Allow 2-3 hours for mountain road transit; conditions vary
days.note: Weather on the high plateaux can mirror Arctic conditions even when lower areas are mild.

days.title: Royal Deeside and Dark Horizons

stops.name: Mar Lodge Estate
stops.detail: Discover a landscape-scale conservation site and explore the upper Deeside hill ranges.

stops.name: Tomintoul and Glenlivet Dark Sky Park
stops.detail: Venture to the most northerly Dark Sky Park in the world for stargazing on vast horizons.

days.driving: Allow 2-3 hours for rural A-road travel; conditions vary
days.note: Dark sky visibility is dependent on seasonal cloud cover and lack of moon glow.

intel.title: Village and Trail Hubs
intel.text: Formal parking is located at main community hubs like Aviemore and specific nature reserve entries. Availability at remote trailheads is not guaranteed during peak summer months.

intel.title: Highland Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular signal is generally available in larger towns such as Kingussie but can be non-existent in deep glens and high plateaux. Prepare offline navigation for mountain routes.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Refuel in gateway towns along the A9 or A93 before entering more remote sectors like Tomintoul. Distances between stations can be significant in the park's interior.

intel.title: Seasonal Wildlife Windows
intel.text: Early morning is optimal for spotting red squirrels or capercaillie in wooded areas. Golden hour viewpoints are best enjoyed during long summer evenings or crisp winter afternoons.

intel.title: Path and Stalking Notices
intel.text: Public access follows the Scottish outdoor access code, though some paths may close for conservation. Check official notices during the deer stalking season.

plan.arrival: Pickup your rental in Inverness or Perth; stock up on regional food like venison or beef in local farms and crofts before checking into Highland lodging.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for main roads like the A9 and A93, but check rental agreements for travel on unpaved estate tracks.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from the Cairngorm Mountain plateau offers views across the granite tors, subject to seasonal visibility.
